newsitem.title: USA: ADM possible settlement delayed - report.
newsitem.headline: ADM possible settlement delayed - report.

text.p: Announcement of a possible settlement between Archer Daniels Midland Co and the U.S. Justice Department in a probe of price fixing in the lysine market may be delayed until next week, according to a broadcast report.
"There had been plans for an announcement as soon as tomorrow, but that has been put off as plea negotiations with ADM continue," according to a report on CNBC, a cable television business channel.

Citing an unidentified source close to the investigation, CNBC said federal prosecutors wanted to press formal charges against the grain processor and its top executives for fixing prices in the lysine market. Lysine is a feed additive.
In addition, CNBC said a new deal is in the works for Mark Whitacre, a former ADM executive turned government informant.
Last year, ADM fired Whitacre, president of its BioProducts division, on allegations he stole millions of dollars from the company.
Citing a source close to the case, CNBC said the federal government would have Whitacre plead guilty to price fixing.
ADM officials were not available to comment on the report.
Late last month, three companies entered pleas of no contest or guilty in a settlement with the U.S. government as part of an antitrust investigation.

Ajinomoto Co Inc pleaded no contest, while Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd of Tokyo and the U.S. unit of Sewon Co Ltd of South Korea, pleaded guilty. In addition, the three agreed to cooperate with testimony and documents as the probe continued.
At the time, legal experts said the companies' cooperation increased the likelihood that ADM would face charges as a result of the investigation.
